title: The holy trumpet gathers the spiritual theater of Easter
english: A holy and royal trumpet for us gathered together this spiritual theater. Bethlehem filled it, and Zion fired it. In it the Cross is the hammer and the Resurrection the anvil. I do not know how to utter its beauty, how to express its light, how to declare the joy within it, or how to recount the kingdom within it. With what hand shall I even touch it?

In what words shall I greet a tomb that begets life, a grave free of corruption yet a procurator of incorruptibility, a bridal chamber that put the Bridegroom to sleep for three days and raised the bride undefiled after the wedding? The tomb under guard proclaimed a dead man, and the earth, shaken, proclaimed God. For his body cries out that he is dead, but the miracle declares God. The burial proclaims him dead, the Resurrection proclaims God. The women's tears treat him as dead, yet the angels' words proclaim God. Joseph buried him as a dead man, yet the one buried
translator_notes: σφῦρα is 'hammer' and ἄκμων 'anvil'; ἐπύρωσεν is 'tempered in fire', as metal is worked in a forge.

μνῆμα φθορᾶς μὲν ἐλεύθερον, ἀφθαρσίας δὲ πρόξενον: 'a grave free of corruption that yet brings about incorruption'. The μὲν is an editor's supplement (set in angle brackets in the edition) and is followed.
παστάδα τριήμερον τὸν νυμφίον κοιμήσασαν: the bridal chamber 'for three days' (τριήμερον) in which the bridegroom slept.
Νεκρὸν ... θεόν: one verb, βοᾷ ('cries out, declares'), governs the whole series, so each pair reads 'declares him dead ... declares him God'.
This section ends in mid-sentence (ἀλλ' ὁ κηδευθεὶς ὡς ἄνθρωπος); the English gives 'as a man' here, and the sentence continues at the start of the next section.
baehrens: PG 93; Homilia ii in sanctum pascha (Khazarzar) u01 open
orientation: Hesychius opens the homily by describing the Easter trumpet that assembles the spiritual theater, filled by Bethlehem and fired by Zion, with the Cross as hammer and Resurrection as anvil, and confesses the impossibility of declaring its beauty, light, joy, and kingdom.
